belief: I'm a failure because I lost my job.
origins: Losing a job can feel personal even when it is not. Layoffs, closures, health problems, and changes in an industry happen to capable people. Yet many of us learned that success means staying employed and that anything else is failure. Shame often arrives faster than the facts, especially if we tied our identity to the job or worry about what family will say.
teaches: Scripture does not treat a fall as the end of a person. Proverbs says that though a righteous man may fall seven times, he still gets up. Micah says, “Though I have fallen, I will rise. Though I sit in darkness, the LORD will be my light.” The psalmist says the Lord is near to the brokenhearted. Falling is part of life, and what makes someone a failure in God’s eyes is not what happened to them but whether they stay down. God stays close in the meantime.
self_statements: If I were better, I would still have my job.
This proves I was never good enough.
Everyone else holds on to their jobs.
I should have seen it coming.
errors: Calling myself “a failure” instead of describing an event.
Taking blame for decisions made by the company or the economy.
Seeing myself as either successful or a failure.
Believing I should have known what I could not have known.
questions: What actually led to the job loss, and which parts were outside my control?
What would I tell a friend who lost a job in the same way?
What skills and accomplishments do I still have?
Where did I learn that losing a job means failing?
What does God say about people who fall?
What is one step I can take to get back up?
truth: Losing a job is something that happened to me, not what I am. I may have things to learn, and some parts may have been outside my control. God is near to me in this season, and I can get up and take the next step.
hw_truths: A job loss is an event, not an identity.
I can fall and still get up.
God is near to the brokenhearted.
I can learn without condemning myself.
I do not have to face this alone.
log: Each day, write one fact about what happened and one thing about yourself that is still true.
actions: Write what happened on one side and what you tell yourself about it on the other.
Write five skills or accomplishments that did not disappear with the job.
Share the whole story and ask for their view.
Update a resume, contact a former coworker, or schedule a conversation.
prayer: Lord, You are near to the brokenhearted. I feel the sting of this loss. Lift me up, remind me who I am in You, and show me the next step. Amen.
hw_questions: What would I say to a friend?
What is still true about me?
What is one step this week?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I can fall and still get up, because the Lord is near.”
